rig.toad: 2017 Jeep Wrangler Unlimited Rubicon JK, automatic

items.text: Confirm site number and that it's a pull-through
items.note: Check-in desk or reservation email.

items.text: Walk the site before driving in
items.note: Find the pedestal, water spigot, and sewer inlet. Look for low branches (you're 11'8"), posts, and slide clearance on both sides.

items.text: Note where hookups sit relative to the coach
items.note: Utilities are on the driver side. Stop so all three reach without extensions.

sections.title: Park and unhook the Jeep
sections.warning: Unhook on level ground with the coach straight. A bound tow bar is hard to release on a curve or slope.

items.text: Stop the coach in a straight line on level ground
items.note: Coach in Park, parking brake set.

items.text: Set the Jeep's parking brake
items.note: Keeps the Jeep from rolling when the arms release.

items.text: Disconnect the lights cord and the breakaway cable
Unplug the Demco Coach Link from the dash outlet
items.note: It only needs power while towing.

items.text: Unhook the crossed safety cables from the baseplate
Release the Avail arms with the black lock levers
items.note: Pull each lever; the arm unlocks and can telescope.

items.text: Pull the pins and clips at the Jeep's baseplate tabs
items.note: Keep the pins and clips together in one pouch.

items.text: Fold the Avail arms up and secure them on the coach
items.note: It stays in the coach receiver. Strap or pin the arms so they don't swing.

items.text: Unplug and stow the baseplate tabs on the Jeep, if removable
Put the Jeep back in drive mode (automatic JK)
items.note: Foot on brake, start engine. Shift transmission to N. Shift transfer case firmly to 2H. Shift transmission to P, then drive.

items.text: Confirm no warning lights and the steering feels normal
Park the Jeep clear of the slides and awning

sections.title: Level and open up
sections.warning: Order matters. Level first, then slides. Extending slides before leveling strains the slide mechanisms.

items.text: Auto-level with the hydraulic jacks
items.note: Engine running, Park, brake on. Use pads under jacks on soft ground or asphalt in heat.

items.text: Chock the wheels
items.note: Belt and suspenders, especially on any slope.

items.text: Check slide clearance, then extend both slides
items.note: Someone outside watches for posts, trees, and the picnic table.

items.text: Turn off the engine

sections.title: Electric
sections.warning: Test before you plug in. A bad pedestal can fry the converter and appliances.

items.text: Turn the pedestal breaker OFF
Plug in the surge protector / EMS and let it test
items.note: Wait for a green light before plugging in the coach.

items.text: Plug in the 30-amp cord, then turn the breaker ON
Confirm shore power inside
items.note: Check the monitor panel and that the charger is running. Generator stays off.

sections.title: Water
sections.warning: Drinking-water hose only. Your city water port sits inches from the black flush port. Blue hose goes to city water, never the left port.

items.text: Flush the spigot for a few seconds
items.note: Clears dirt and stale water.

items.text: Attach pressure regulator (and filter) at the spigot
items.note: Keeps park pressure under about 50 psi.

items.text: Connect the blue potable hose to CITY WATER
items.note: The right-hand port, labeled city water.

items.text: Turn the spigot on slowly and check for leaks
Turn the 12V water pump OFF
items.note: On city water you don't need it.

items.text: Open a hot faucet until water runs steadily
items.note: Purges air from the water heater.

items.text: Then turn on the water heater
items.note: Never heat an empty or air-filled heater.

sections.title: Sewer
sections.warning: Black valve stays closed until it's ⅔ full. Open black valves let liquids drain and leave solids behind.

items.text: Put on gloves
Connect sewer hose to the coach, then to the inlet
items.note: Use a sewer donut if the park requires it. Set up the hose support so it slopes downhill.

items.text: Confirm black valve is CLOSED
Gray valve: closed or cracked open
items.note: Closed saves gray water to rinse the hose on dump day.

items.text: Open the propane service valve (gray knob in the tank bay)
items.note: Turn slowly counterclockwise.

items.text: Set the refrigerator to AUTO / electric
items.note: Shore power saves propane.

items.text: Set thermostat or A/C as needed

sections.title: Outside setup
sections.warning: Awning and wind: Retract it any time wind picks up or you leave the site.

items.text: Extend the awning
items.note: Check for branches overhead first.

items.text: Set out the mat, chairs, and griddle
Set up the satellite dish
items.note: Needs a clear view of the southern sky. Aim it with the app or auto-seek, then connect the coax to the satellite input.

items.text: Walk around once more
items.note: Look for drips at every connection.

items.text: Open roof vents and turn on fans
Release fridge and cabinet travel latches
Set up TV input and check Wi-Fi or cell signal
Check the weather and route
items.note: Low clearances, propane restrictions (for example, I-695 Baltimore tunnels), and fuel stops with pull-through canopies.

items.text: Dump and flush the tanks if leaving early
items.note: Black first, then flush, then gray. Or do it in the morning.

items.text: Decide on fresh water for travel
items.note: Carry ⅓ tank or less to save weight, unless your next stop is dry camping.

sections.title: Dump and flush
sections.warning: Black valve open before you run the flush. Flushing into a closed tank backs sewage up into the toilet.

items.text: Gloves on
Open the BLACK valve and drain
items.note: Wait until the clear elbow slows.

items.text: Connect the separate flush hose to the LEFT port and flush 5–10 min
items.note: Stay with it. Stop when the elbow runs clear.

items.text: Close the black valve
Open the GRAY valve and drain it
items.note: Soapy water rinses the hose.

items.text: Close the gray valve
Add 2–3 gal of water and enzyme treatment to the black tank
Rinse, cap, and stow the sewer hose and flush hose
items.note: Keep them apart from the drinking hose.

items.text: Turn off the water heater
Turn off the spigot
Relieve pressure by opening a faucet briefly
Disconnect and drain the blue hose, regulator, and filter; stow
Cap the city water port

sections.title: Inside
sections.warning: Everything that can move, will. Walk every room.

items.text: Close and latch all cabinets, drawers, and the fridge
Stow loose items on counters, the table, and the shower
Close roof vents, windows, and blinds
Turn off fans, lights, TV, and A/C
Set the fridge for travel
items.note: Leave it on propane or battery only if your propane plan allows. Many close propane for tunnels and ferries.

items.text: Water pump OFF
Retract the awning
Stow the satellite dish and disconnect its coax
Stow chairs, mat, griddle, and any tools
Close the propane service valve if required for your route
items.note: Required for some tunnels and ferries.

items.text: Turn the pedestal breaker OFF
Unplug the coach cord and the surge protector; stow both
Confirm the coach batteries are charged

sections.title: Slides and jacks
sections.warning: Slides in before jacks up. Keep people and the dog clear.

items.text: Engine running, Park, brake set
Retract both slides fully
items.note: Watch for anything caught in the slide seals.

items.text: Retract the leveling jacks
items.note: Confirm on the panel that all jacks are up.

items.text: Pull the wheel chocks and jack pads

sections.title: Hook up the Jeep
sections.warning: Order matters on the JK. Never shift into Park with the transfer case in Neutral while the engine is running.

items.text: Line up the Jeep behind the coach
items.note: Straight and close enough for the Avail arms to reach the baseplate tabs.

items.text: Unfold the Avail arms and pin them to the baseplate tabs
items.note: Insert both pins and lock both clips.

items.text: Attach the safety cables, crossed under the tow bar
Connect the lights cord and the breakaway cable
items.note: The lights cord also powers the Demco brake system in the Jeep.

items.text: Put the Jeep in flat-tow mode (automatic JK)
items.note: Key to ACC. Foot on brake, parking brake set. Transmission to N. Transfer case to N.

items.text: Verify the transfer case is in Neutral
items.note: Start the engine. Shift the transmission to D and release the brake. The Jeep must not move.

items.text: Finish flat-tow mode
items.note: Engine OFF, key in the unlocked OFF position so the steering turns. Transmission to P.

items.text: Release the Jeep's parking brake
items.note: Easy to forget. It will destroy the rear brakes.

items.text: Switch ON the Demco brake unit in the Jeep
items.note: Controller faces the direction of travel, switch toward the driver's seat.

items.text: Test the Jeep's brake lights and turn signals
items.note: Have someone watch.

items.text: Plug the Demco Coach Link into the coach's 12V outlet
items.note: Power light on. Press the coach brake: the Brakes Applied lights should light and beep. No lights means no toad brakes.

items.text: Pull forward slowly until both Avail arms lock
items.note: You'll hear them click. Check both lock indicators.

sections.title: Final walk-around
sections.warning: Last lap saves the most money. Do it every single time.

items.text: All compartments closed and locked
Entry step retracted
Tire check
items.note: Coach 75 psi front / 80 psi rear, Jeep 37 psi, all cold. Check the TPMS display for all 10 tires.

items.text: Nothing left at the site
items.note: Check the pedestal, spigot, sewer inlet, and picnic table.

items.text: Mirrors, GPS with the RV profile, and seatbelts
